standard.title: Consumer and Financial Rights and Responsibilities
standard.description: the rights and responsibilities of individuals and businesses in relation to consumer and financial products and services
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored consumer choices and strategies for making informed financial decisions (AC9HS6K08) and are developing understanding of work and income (AC9HE7K04). They are familiar with making purchases but have not formally examined the legal and ethical framework of rights and responsibilities that governs consumer and financial transactions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the rights and responsibilities of individuals and businesses in relation to consumer and financial products and services.

nodes.label: Rights versus responsibilities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish between rights and responsibilities, and apply this distinction to consumer and financial contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Distinguish rights from responsibilities with a clear definition; give one consumer example of each.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish rights (entitlements that can be claimed) from responsibilities (obligations that must be met) in everyday language; develop a list of rights and responsibilities for both individuals and businesses in consumer and financial contexts.
wider: Examine how consumer rights vary across different contexts — for example, purchasing from a large corporation versus a local market stallholder, or buying online versus in-store
Explore how the concept of rights and responsibilities was codified in Australian consumer law — what prompted the development of formal consumer protections?
Investigate how consumer rights differ for First Nations communities in remote areas accessing goods through community stores, and what responsibilities fall on those store operators
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot distinguish rights from responsibilities at the conceptual level, they will not be able to correctly assign rights and responsibilities to parties in specific consumer scenarios in subsequent nodes. The distinction underpins all analysis of who is entitled to what and who is obligated to whom.

response_modes.reason: Students often conflate rights and responsibilities or use them interchangeably. Scaffold with a clear definitional contrast — a right is something you can claim; a responsibility is something you must fulfil — then apply to concrete examples where the parties are identifiable.

success_criteria: Defines rights and responsibilities in own words with a clear distinction
Gives one example of a consumer right and one consumer responsibility for an individual

nodes.label: Individual rights in consumer and financial contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the rights of individuals in relation to consumer and financial products and services, including warranties, cooling-off periods and return processes.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain two individual consumer rights — such as the right to a warranty or a cooling-off period — with a concrete example of how each applies.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the rights of individuals in relation to consumer and financial products and services including: warranties, cooling-off periods, and processes for returning goods; apply each right to a realistic consumer scenario.
wider: Investigate the Australian Consumer Law and identify at least three consumer rights it codifies — examining how the law translates abstract rights into enforceable protections
Explore how digital purchases (apps, subscriptions, online goods) create consumer rights questions that differ from traditional in-store purchases
Examine how consumers can exercise their rights in practice — who to contact, what to say, and what documentation to keep — developing a practical guide for a Year 7 audience

response_modes.reason: Students need concrete exposure to specific rights before they can reason about how rights and responsibilities balance. Build a set of scenario cards — each presenting a consumer situation — and have students identify which right applies and how to exercise it.

success_criteria: Explains at least two individual consumer rights with a concrete example of each
Describes what a warranty or cooling-off period is and when it applies

nodes.label: Business responsibilities and product safety
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the responsibilities of businesses in relation to consumer and financial products and services, including mandatory and voluntary standards and product safety recalls.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two business responsibilities in consumer or financial contexts with a concrete example; explain what happens when a business fails to meet these responsibilities.
nodes.typical_width: Explain business responsibilities in consumer and financial contexts including: mandatory and voluntary standards, product safety recalls, and obligations to provide accurate information; apply to real-world examples of businesses meeting or failing their responsibilities.
wider: Analyse a real product safety recall — what triggered it, what the business was responsible for doing, and what the consequences were for consumers and the business
Compare mandatory versus voluntary standards: why would a business voluntarily adopt standards beyond legal requirements? What incentives exist?
Investigate the responsibilities of a financial services business (such as a bank) toward its customers — exploring how these differ from general product responsibilities

response_modes.reason: Product recalls, financial services responsibilities and voluntary standards are sufficiently different in mechanism and consequence that separate concrete examples are needed for each. Students who only see one context will not be able to explain the range of business responsibilities.

success_criteria: Explains at least two business responsibilities with a real example of each
Describes what a product safety recall is and what the business is responsible for doing

nodes.label: Budgeting, decision-making and integration
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how developing personal or business budgets and savings plans supports better decision-making about consumer and financial products and services, integrating rights and responsibilities into that framework.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain why a budget or savings plan is useful before making a consumer or financial decision; link this to one right or responsibility identified in prior nodes.
nodes.typical_width: Explain the importance of budgets and savings plans for individuals and businesses as a foundation for informed consumer and financial decisions; connect budgeting to exercising consumer rights responsibly (e.g. not over-committing, understanding what you've agreed to); apply to a realistic decision scenario.
wider: Develop a simple personal budget for a hypothetical consumer decision and map the rights and responsibilities that apply at each stage of the purchase

Examine how access to budgeting and financial literacy tools differs across communities — including remote and First Nations communities — and what this means for exercising consumer rights effectively
Investigate how businesses use budgets and financial planning to meet their responsibilities to consumers — for example, setting aside funds for warranty claims or recalls

response_modes.reason: This node coordinates rights, responsibilities and financial decision-making into a coherent whole. Students should be able to reason: informed decision-making depends on both knowing your rights and planning your finances — these reinforce each other.

success_criteria: Explains why a budget or savings plan supports better consumer or financial decisions
Connects the budgeting rationale to at least one consumer right or business responsibility
Uses relevant terms (rights, responsibilities, warranty, budget, standards, product safety) accurately
